court: In the High Court of Madras
respondents: Inspector General of Registration and Others … Respondent(s).
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. P. Harish for R 1 to R 3
judgment_text:
Writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking for issuance of a writ of mandamus to direct the respondents 1 to 3 to dispose of the petitioner's representation dated 16-2-2026 objection from registering the document in Survey No. 16/8 to an extent of 0.40 cents, situated at Ananthapuram village, Arakkonam Taluk, Ranipet District expeditiously in accordance with law.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

Abdul Quddhose, J.:— The grievance of the petitioner in this writ petition is that due to an inadvertent mistake, the property belonging to the petitioner has been included in the UDR patta issued to the respondents 4 to 6. Therefore, according to the petitioner, the third respondent shall not register any document pertaining to the petitioner's property. The petitioner has already filed a protest petition before the third respondent opposing for registration of the document in respect of the subject property.

2. Mr P. Harish, learned government advocate, accepts notice on behalf of the respondents 1 to 3, and on instructions, submits that the third respondent shall hear the petitioner before taking a final decision as to whether any document presented by the respondents 4 to 6 pertaining to the subject property can be registered or not.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner is also satisfied with the submissions made by the learned government advocate for the official respondents.

4. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of by directing the third respondent to issue notice to the petitioner as and when any document is presented for registration by any of the private respondents, namely, respondents 4 to 6, pertaining to the subject property, and only after hearing the objections of the petitioner and after giving due consideration to the same, the third respondent is permitted to register any document presented by any of the private respondents for registration. Since no adverse orders are passed against the respondents 4 to 6, notice to them in this writ petition is dispensed with by this Court. No Costs.
